title: Copilot Studio: block sharing of agents that embed maker credentials
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap record and Microsoft Learn. The administrative routes, sharing-limits command, preview default and product licensing are documented; the page distinguishes publish-time enforcement from existing access and runtime behaviour.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Copilot Studio evaluates agent connections and can prevent unsafe sharing or publishing.
claims.quote: It lets Copilot Studio evaluate the connections used by an agent and can prevent the agent from being shared or published when a connection violates the organization's connection-sharing policy.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; controls[0].governs
claims.claim: Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials is an environment-level control for Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: The Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials setting is an environment-level control for Microsoft Copilot Studio agents.

claims.where: summary; What's changing
claims.claim: Embedded maker credentials are supplied at design time and can be used when the agent runs.
claims.quote: These embedded maker credentials are supplied at design time and can be used when the agent runs.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Other users of an agent using a maker connection can perform operations with the maker's permissions.
claims.quote: When an agent uses such a connection, other users of the agent can perform operations by using the permissions associated with the maker's credentials.

claims.where: What's changing: unsafe-sharing conditions
claims.claim: An unsafe-sharing condition is that the agent uses at least one connection that does not allow credential sharing.
claims.quote: An agent is considered unsafe for sharing when both of the following conditions are true: ... The agent uses at least one connection that doesn’t allow credential sharing.

claims.where: What's changing: unsafe-sharing conditions
claims.claim: The other required unsafe-sharing condition is design-time credentials rather than each user's own authentication.
claims.quote: An agent is considered unsafe for sharing when both of the following conditions are true: ... The connection uses credentials supplied at design time instead of asking each user to authenticate with their own credentials.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: As dependency-based enforcement becomes available, a called flow or agent with a nonshareable connection can make the parent unsafe.
claims.quote: For example, an agent might call a flow or another agent that uses a nonshareable connection. As dependency-based enforcement becomes available, an unsafe dependency can cause the calling agent to be treated as unsafe for sharing.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: Connections configured to use end-user credentials are not subject to this connection-sharing restriction.
claims.quote: Connections configured to use end-user credentials aren't subject to this connection-sharing restriction because each user authenticates by using their own connection at runtime.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The configuration article documents two modes named All sharing allowed and Safe sharing enforced.
claims.quote: The control provides two modes. Choose the mode that matches the environment's risk tolerance and rollout stage. ... All sharing allowed ... Safe sharing enforced

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: All sharing allowed detects unsafe credential use and informs makers.
claims.quote: All sharing allowed | Copilot Studio detects and informs makers about unsafe credential use, but doesn’t block sharing.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: All sharing allowed does not block sharing.
claims.quote: All sharing allowed | Copilot Studio detects and informs makers about unsafe credential use, but doesn’t block sharing.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Safe sharing enforced blocks applicable publish or share paths for unsafe agents.
claims.quote: Safe sharing enforced | Copilot Studio blocks applicable publish or share paths when an agent is unsafe for sharing.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Makers can still edit an unsafe agent in enforced mode.
claims.quote: When Safe sharing enforced is selected, makers can still edit and save an unsafe agent, but they can't newly share it.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Makers can still save an unsafe agent in enforced mode.
claims.quote: When Safe sharing enforced is selected, makers can still edit and save an unsafe agent, but they can't newly share it.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Makers cannot newly share an unsafe agent when Safe sharing enforced is selected.
claims.quote: When Safe sharing enforced is selected, makers can still edit and save an unsafe agent, but they can't newly share it.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: An agent violating the policy cannot be shared with everyone in the organisation for end-user access.
claims.quote: Similarly, you can't share the agent with everyone in your organization for end-user access.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Some channels distribute the agent through publishing without a separate Share action.
claims.quote: Some channels make an agent available as part of publishing and don’t provide a separate Share action. In these scenarios, enforcement occurs primarily when the maker publishes the agent.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: In publish-based distribution scenarios, maker user credentials at runtime disable publishing while enforcement is active.
claims.quote: If the agent uses the maker’s user credentials at runtime, Copilot Studio marks the agent as unsafe and disables publishing while enforcement is active.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: An authenticated agent that has not been shared can publish successfully under enforcement.
claims.quote: For authenticated agents, an agent that you didn't share can publish successfully, while an agent you already shared with another user is blocked from publishing when enforcement applies.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: Later publishing of an already-shared agent can be blocked if it still has unsafe embedded maker credentials.
claims.quote: A later publish of an already-shared agent can be blocked if the agent still contains unsafe embedded maker credentials.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: An approved system identity such as a service principal, API key or managed identity can permit publishing when the connection supports the scenario.
claims.quote: Agents that use an approved system identity, such as a service principal, API key, or managed identity, can be published when the associated connection supports the scenario.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Enabling this control does not retroactively unshare or disable previously shared agents.
claims.quote: Enabling enforcement doesn’t retroactively unshare or disable agents that were previously shared.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The safe-sharing control governs sharing and publishing, not blocking an agent while it runs.
claims.quote: The sharing agents with embedded maker credentials control governs sharing and publishing. It doesn’t block an agent while the agent is running.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Tools affected by a connection-sharing violation are marked Blocked.
claims.quote: Makers can see which tools are affected. These tools are marked as Blocked with a Sharing policy violation message explaining that a connection violates the administrator's connection-sharing policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Affected tools show a Sharing policy violation message.
claims.quote: These tools are marked as Blocked with a Sharing policy violation message explaining that a connection violates the administrator's connection-sharing policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: If a tool is also restricted by a data policy, the displayed message is Data policy violation instead.
claims.quote: If a tool is also restricted by a data policy, Copilot Studio surfaces the Data policy violation message instead.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; What's changing
claims.claim: The Publish option is unavailable for a blocking condition under enforcement, subject to the authenticated-unshared exception stated in What's changing.
claims.quote: When Copilot Studio detects a blocking condition before publishing, the Publish option is unavailable and makers are directed to review the agent's status.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: A violating agent cannot be shared with a user who has viewer or end-user access.
claims.quote: You can't share an agent that violates a connection-sharing security policy with a user who has viewer or end-user access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Dependency-based enforcement can expand over time.
claims.quote: Dependency-based enforcement can expand over time. Include called agents and flows in your governance and testing process.

claims.where: Scope: Who and what
claims.claim: Dependencies in other environments or tenants can require additional validation.
claims.quote: Evaluate each environment separately. Agents and flows that depend on components in other environments or tenants can require additional validation.
